items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec>
<jats:title>Background</jats:title>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Spartina alterniflora</jats:italic> is an invasive plant on the coast of China that replaces native vegetation and has a serious negative impact on local ecosystems. Monitoring the spatial distribution of <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> and its changes over time can reveal its expansion mechanism, which is crucial for the management of coastal ecosystems. The purpose of this study was to map the distribution of <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> in Zhejiang Province from 1985 to 2015 using a time series of Landsat TM/OLI images and analyze the temporal and spatial patterns of expansion of this species.</jats:p>
</jats:sec><jats:sec>
<jats:title>Results</jats:title>
<jats:p>After analyzing the distribution of coastal vegetation, the vegetation index was calculated based on Landsat images for 4 years (1985, 1995, 2005 and 2015). According to a threshold determined based on expert knowledge, the distribution of <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> in Zhejiang Province was extracted, and the temporal and spatial changes in the distribution of <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> were analyzed. The classification accuracy was 90.3%. <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> has expanded rapidly in recent decades after being introduced into southern Zhejiang. Between 1985 and 2015, <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> increased its area of distribution by 10,000 hm<jats:sup>2</jats:sup>, and it replaced native vegetation to become the most abundant halophyte in tidal flats. Overall, <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> expanded from south to north over the decades of the study, and the fastest expansion rate was 463.64 hm<jats:sup>2</jats:sup>/year, which occurred between 1995 and 2005. <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> was widely distributed in the tidal flats of bays and estuaries and expanded outward as sediment accumulated.</jats:p>
</jats:sec><jats:sec>
<jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
<jats:p>This study reveals the changes over time in <jats:italic>S. alterniflora</jats:italic> cover in Zhejiang and can contribute to the control and management of this invasive plant.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
title: Monitoring of the invasion of Spartina alterniflora from 1985 to 2015 in Zhejiang Province, China

items.abstract: <jats:p>The annual rates and depth distribution of organic carbon mineralization to CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> were determined in sediments supporting stands of short Spartina alterniflora. Carbon dioxide production was estimated by two independent techniques. We constructed a CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> budget based on measurements of CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> emission from the sediment to the atmosphere, export of dissolved inorganic carbon in porewater exchange, and changes in the porewater pool of dissolved inorganic carbon throughout the year. We also measured CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> production in salt marsh sediments by monitoring changes in total inorganic carbon in cores. The estimates obtained by the two methods were similar, giving a total annual CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> production of between 67 and 70 mol°m<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>2</jats:sup>°yr<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>1</jats:sup>. We also measured the losses of organic matter as methane (O.1—0.3 mol°m<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>2</jats:sup>°yr<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>1</jats:sup>) and dissolved organic carbon (0—3 mol°m<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>2</jats:sup>°yr<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>1</jats:sup>) and burial (7.4 mol°m<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>2</jats:sup>°yr<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>1</jats:sup>) in order to construct a carbon budget for the sediments. These data, when combined with the estimates of carbon mineralization, gave an estimate for the organic carbon loading to the sediments of 68—78 mol°m<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>2</jats:sup>°yr<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>1</jats:sup>. About 95% of the annual carbon input either decomposes to CO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> in situ or is buried, and <5% is exported from the sediment. We estimated that belowground C production in short S. alterniflora in this Massachusetts marsh is 58—75 mol°m<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>2</jats:sup>°yr<jats:sup>—</jats:sup><jats:sup>1</jats:sup>.</jats:p>
